From a candidate dataset to an Atlas source

Loading the catalog…

The RL Data Atlas lists every RL task source that Marin has declared, with its review state and evidence. A source is one pinned population of tasks, for example one Hugging Face dataset revision. A task is one RL problem stored as a TaskSpec: the prompt, the machine environment the agent works in, the answer contract and the grader (also called the verifier).

This page shows each path a dataset can take into the Atlas and what each outcome lets you rely on. The counts come from the catalog snapshot that the Atlas currently serves, so they change when an operator loads a new snapshot. The normative rules live in the task curation reference; each step below links to its section and to the code that enforces it.

The paths

Select an outcome to list its sources. Agentic tasks need a machine (a shell, files or tools); reply-only and conversation tasks skip steps 2 and 3.

What each outcome guarantees

Admitted is the only outcome a training run can use, and only after a selection recipe names the source. The Daytona label applies to admitted and runnable sources; it describes where a source can run, not whether it is admitted.

OutcomeYou can rely onYou cannot rely onSources
Rejected Nothing from it reaches training. A rejected agentic source fails runnable_sources(). A rejected task is a typed rejection whose reason the source manifest.json counts. Seeing it as a row here. Task-level rejections appear only in the source manifest and its Atlas source details. —
Inventory only A pinned reference, a declared row count where known and any independent QC that the upstream release recorded. Any execution evidence. Quality shows Not assessed. The source cannot be selected for training.
Grandfathered blend The same rows that the historical Nemotron Ultra mix used. The list is frozen, so no new source can join it. A measured environment, a snapshot count or the environment-fidelity rules. These blends predate them and are out of the current audit's scope.
Runnable, oversight not declared The source passed the format gate. A non-agentic source's admission rests on its campaign record (panel review and controls), shown in its source details. A declared oversight level or its evidence pointers. An agentic source in this state is class (b) and needs SAMPLE or FULL QA to stay runnable. Snapshots loaded before the oversight field existed put every runnable source here.
Excluded The source notes say which defect or duplicate the review found. Its history stays in the Atlas. Any of its tasks in a run. Excluded sources are not runnable.
Deprecated A named replacement or withdrawal reason in the notes, and the retained history. Any of its tasks in a run. runnable_sources() drops deprecated sources.
Admitted, SAMPLE Every task passed the mechanical admission checks, including environment fidelity. Controls, verifier execution and a blinded review passed on a documented sample. The evidence names the campaign, recipe revision and verification summary. That every task's verifier works. Unsampled tasks were not executed one by one.
Admitted, FULL Every task ran end to end, including its verifier. Grader correctness beyond the controls and review: a live verifier can still mis-grade. Selection checks exact overlap with the heldout set; it does not do semantic decontamination.
Daytona safe
The source's tasks need at most the snapshot limit of unique environments, and Daytona accepts every task's execution requirements.
Daytona unsafe
A run would exceed the snapshot limit or ask for something Daytona refuses. The source stays ingested; run it on gVisor or the local backend, or rebuild it faithfully.
Unassessed
An agentic source without a measurement. Its Daytona behavior is unknown.

The steps in detail

1 Declare the source

Each dataset is one RlDataSource in a module under datasets/, collected by all_sources() in sources.py. Its SourceInfo gives a stable ID, a title, an origin, a family, search tags and notes. Its input is pinned to an immutable revision. A source without a pipeline is Inventory: listed with its evidence, never admitted. The tag deprecated marks it Deprecated and excluded marks it Excluded; the notes carry the reason.

Rule: Declarations. Code: source.py.

2 Task format gate

An agentic source declares SourceInfo.task_format. A new agentic source must ingest TaskCompendium or Harbor task directories: a directory per task with task.toml, its environment and its verifier. MARINSKYRL, Marin's internal blend format, is accepted only for the sources in GRANDFATHERED_MARINSKYRL_SOURCES, a frozen list of Nemotron Ultra components admitted before the requirement. Selection raises for any other agentic source, so it fails before a run starts.

Rule: Declarations. Code: require_accepted_task_format in sources.py.

3 Environment fidelity

An agentic task's environment specification is part of the data. The task runs in exactly the environment its source specifies: built from the archive's own Dockerfile (docker_build), or lowered exactly onto a digest-pinned base, with each RUN as a setup command and the recipe's working directory and environment variables. A recipe the lowering cannot express is refused. A shared image such as iris-task never stands in for a task's environment. The one exception: when provably_no_op_against proves the Dockerfile changes nothing relative to that image, the task may declare the image, and the change ships as a new dataset version.

An agentic task that declares no environment is rejected; it would otherwise run in the host image. A source declaration cannot supply the missing environment.

A source is repaired when its published spec completely describes how its tasks run. A conversion may change delivery at ingestion, for example a reply-only rewrite that grades the assistant response in place of /app/answer.txt, but only with SAMPLE or FULL QA behind it. Audits sort sources into three classes:

  • (a) OK The spec describes runtime behavior and SAMPLE or FULL QA evidence exists.
  • (b) Needs QA The spec describes runtime behavior, but QA evidence is missing.
  • (c) Needs repair Runtime behavior differs from the spec: a substituted image, a missing environment resolved to the host, or a declared environment that the conversion ignores.

Rule: Environment fidelity and repair. Code: environment_fidelity.py (lower_environment, provably_no_op_against, missing_environment, environment_unused).

4 Curation modes and oversight

The curation driver requires --mode quick|sample|full. QUICK converts rows to TaskSpecs and records typed rejections; it reviews nothing and admits nothing, so a QUICK-only source has oversight none and stays inventory. SAMPLE reviews a bounded panel of at most 100 rows. FULL expands an accepted source to every row and verifies the kept tasks.

Each source also declares an oversight level, none, sample or full, with evidence that points at the campaign, recipe revision and verification summary. The level is the weakest review the admission rests on. A cohort whose setup ran on every task but whose verifier liveness ran on a sample is sample. Independent QC by the upstream release does not raise the level.

Rule: Curation modes and oversight levels. Code: CurationMode, OversightLevel and OversightEvidence in finestore.rl.curation.

5 Qualify the source

SAMPLE or FULL QA must establish each of these, and the oversight evidence points at the result:

  • Conversion fidelity. Converted TaskSpecs match the archive's instruction, answer contract, environment and grader.
  • Controls. A golden or reference answer scores 1 wherever the source has one. An empty or wrong answer scores 0. An empty answer that scores above 0 marks the task defective (check:empty). A grader that crashes or writes no reward is an infrastructure error, never a zero.
  • Verifier execution. A reward of 0 alone does not prove the verifier ran. Without an oracle, the liveness check requires exit code 0 and a trailing numeric reward below 1 on the untouched workspace.
  • Blinded review of a frozen sample, at least 20 tasks for SAMPLE, finds no systematic mis-grading. The audit-grader method estimates the error rate.
  • Drop accounting. input_rows equals converted rows plus rejections, and every rejection has a reason.
  • Decontamination. Overlap with the tracked evaluation sets is checked where a path exists, and reported as unchecked otherwise.

Sources without oracle solutions

When no row ships a solution, three checks replace the golden control. Payload preservation (offline): every file the native recipe copies appears in the rebuilt setup with identical bytes and mode. Setup execution (local Docker): the lowered setup commands, run in the declared base image, write those same files. Verifier liveness (sandbox): the task's own verifier runs in its graded environment on the untouched workspace and returns a well-formed negative verdict. A crash, timeout, unparsable report or positive reward is a failure. Every sampled task must pass, 20 per base image by default. The result sets oracle_validation:

  • executed: shipped oracle solutions ran and scored their expected reward.
  • verifier_executed: no oracle exists, and the checks above passed. Successful solutions are not certified.
  • skipped: neither ran, so execution is not certified. This is the default for a source without oracles.

Rule: Sources without oracle solutions. Code: no_oracle_qualification.py, no_oracle_liveness.py.

LLM-judged sources

An LLM judge is part of a task's grading semantics. A judged task whose judge model is empty, or whose rubric and settings are unstated, does not describe what grades it, so the source stays at oversight none. The repairer judges ten tasks from the frozen sample by hand, then pins the source to a tier in JUDGE_TIERS: LIGHT for surface checks with a clear contract, MEDIUM for comparison with a reference or checklist, HEAVY for multi-step verification that needs deep domain reasoning. Every tier sets temperature 0.7, or records API default where the API cannot take a temperature.

The judge specification states the rubric, what the judge sees (question, answer, references, context and whether reasoning is removed), the context length, completion tokens and reasoning effort, the harness (API, prompts, label parsing), the turns, the request timeout and the retry budget. It says nothing about the endpoint: a hosted provider, a relay or a local server that serves the named model are interchangeable, and JudgeConnection supplies the URL and key at run time. End-to-end validation through the production grader must show a reference scores 1, a wrong or empty answer scores 0, agreement with the hand verdicts and a blinded review, and a parsed verdict for every request.

Rule: LLM-judged sources. Code: JUDGE_TIERS in experiments/post_training/task_curation/judges.py.

6 Daytona safety

Marin's RL rollouts can run on Daytona, a hosted sandbox service whose organization caps how many snapshots (prebuilt environments) exist at once. A source is unsafe when its tasks need more unique snapshots than the limit, or when Daytona refuses any task's declared execution requirements. The count is measured from the converted agent and grader specs through the same snapshot_identity function that the Daytona factory uses to name snapshots; it makes no Daytona API calls and is never declared by hand. A grader placed by a package lock runs in the local bubblewrap runtime on the worker, which Daytona cannot provision. An unsafe source stays ingested with its label.

Rule: Declarations, Making a dataset Daytona-safe. Code: daytona_identity.py, daytona_verdict in finestore.rl.curation.

7 Publish, deprecate and load

A conversion publishes its cohort to the open-athena Hugging Face organization as a private repository named open-athena/<family>-<format>-<YYYYMMDD>, in TaskCompendium format. The card records provenance, excluded counts with reasons, the license and a research-artifact warning. Verification reads the upload back through the same login and compares file hashes. The Atlas entry points at that repository and revision, with the upstream dataset as provenance.

A published cohort enters the catalog through an importer that converts nothing: import_prebuilt validates every TaskCompendium row under the admission predicates, and import_harbor_prebuilt requires a scored control receipt in controls.jsonl for every native Harbor package. When a qualified release replaces an older source, the older source gets the deprecated tag and a note that names its replacement.

A FULL campaign with --publish-catalog writes the shared catalog. The Atlas changes only when an operator runs its loader on that snapshot.

Rule: Declarations, Updating Atlas. Code: prebuilt.py, campaign_releases.py.

After admission: selection

Admission does not put a source in a training run. A selection recipe (--selection RECIPE.json) names the sources and family quotas and pins a heldout set. Selection reads only final/*.parquet from sources whose manifests record mode: full. Before sampling it removes tasks that match the complete heldout set by task ID, public text or exact conversation, and duplicates across sources. These are exact overlap checks.

Rule: Final task selection. Code: inventory.py. Recipe example: quick RL loop.

Add a source in practice

Access you need

  1. All stages: Python 3.12 or later, uv and Git. Clone the repository and run uv sync --all-packages (installation guide).
  2. QUICK: a local computer. Public sources need no Hugging Face token.
  3. SAMPLE with review: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for a GLM-compatible review model. Pass --base-url, --model (default glm-5.3) and --model-revision, and put the key in GLM_BULK_TOKEN. Without --base-url the driver looks up Marin's internal relay job, which works only inside Marin's Iris cluster.
  4. FULL and production: Iris access (authentication) and CoreWeave object-storage credentials in CW_KEY_ID and CW_KEY_SECRET.
  5. Executable-environment cohorts: a Docker daemon, or a Linux dev box (below).

Marin team members can check everything at once with the onboard-marin skill. Never print a token or key in a log, report or commit.

Your first source

  1. Declare it. Follow adding a dataset: add one RlDataSource to the nearest family module, pin its input, set config=CurationRecipe(...) and pipeline=process_rows, record the license in the notes, and register a new module in all_sources(). Agentic sources also declare task_format.
  2. Test the conversion with a behavioral test in the family's test module: 
    uv run --with-editable './lib/taskcompendium[pipeline]' pytest \
  experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_<family>.py \
  experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_catalog.py
  3. Find the invocation name. --source takes config.name, not the stable ID: 
    uv run python -c 'from experiments.post_training.task_curation.sources import runnable_sources; print("\n".join(runnable_sources()))'
  4. Run QUICK locally and check that input_rows in each manifest.json equals converted_rows plus the sum of rejections: 
    uv run --with-editable './lib/taskcompendium[pipeline]' python \
  -m experiments.post_training.task_curation.driver --mode quick --run \
  --source YOUR_SOURCE --output-root /tmp/task-curation-first
  5. Run SAMPLE with review. A 5-row panel is a fast test; the default is 100. 
    uv run --with-editable './lib/taskcompendium[pipeline]' python \
  -m experiments.post_training.task_curation.driver \
  --mode sample --cache-dir ~/.cache/marin/rl-curation \
  --source YOUR_SOURCE --quality-sample-size 5 --assess \
  --review-mode chat --model-revision GLM_REVISION --base-url GLM_ENDPOINT --run

Debug on a Linux dev box

Bubblewrap graders, Docker inside a pod and verifier liveness need Linux. scripts/iris/dev_cpu.py holds a privileged, non-preemptible CPU pod on a CoreWeave cluster, with the same container profile as curation workers. Name, size, priority and lifetime have no defaults. allocate returns once the pod runs; Iris ends the holder at --max-lifetime.

uv run python -m scripts.iris.dev_cpu --config lib/iris/config/cw-rno2a.yaml --name NAME \
  allocate --cpu 16 --memory 64GB --disk 200GB --priority interactive --max-lifetime 259200
uv run python -m scripts.iris.dev_cpu --name NAME exec -- bash -lc 'bwrap --version; docker info'
uv run python -m scripts.iris.dev_cpu --name NAME cp-to ./grader.py /tmp/grader.py
uv run python -m scripts.iris.dev_cpu --name NAME release

Reference: CPU dev boxes.

Run a production FULL campaign

Run FULL in an Iris job. Keep the SAMPLE run's --quality-sample-size and --seed so FULL reviews the same panel. Omit --run to print the plan with every resolved default. --publish-catalog requires FULL with assessment and no --cache-dir.

uv run iris --cluster=marin job run --target-cluster YOUR-CW-REGION \
  --extra cpu --cpu 0.5 --memory 2GB --timeout 259200 \
  -e GLM_BULK_TOKEN "$GLM_BULK_TOKEN" -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET 1 \
  -- python -m experiments.post_training.task_curation.driver \
  --mode full --source YOUR_SOURCE \
  --review-mode chat --model-revision GLM_REVISION \
  --report-path s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/campaigns/YYYY-MM-DD-N/campaign.json \
  --publish-catalog s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production --run

Iris runs default to 64 workers, a 16g coordinator, 32 normalized shards and the review cache <artifact-root>/rl-data/review-cache, whose keys hash the model revision and the complete request. Without --worker-image, workers use the cluster's default_task_image; pass a digest to record an exact image in the artifact identity.

Read the campaign report before loading: a failed FULL campaign also publishes a snapshot. Then load the Atlas:

uv run python infra/marina/apps/rl_data_catalog/load.py \
  --app-id fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f

Reference: Run a campaign, reviewed local loop, Updating Atlas.

Executable-environment cohorts

Some cohorts need live containers and hidden-test separation, with positive and negative controls before any task is trusted. These authoring tools write everything under the --output you choose and register nothing as training-approved:

  • Staged SWE-Smith: swesmith_staged pilots one parent (--pilot TASK:IMPORT:DEPENDENCY_COMMAND), swesmith_staged_cohort extends validated repositories, swesmith_staged_v2 builds shared-image repair handoffs, and swesmith_handoff validates a submitted workspace against the private contract. Gold patches and contracts stay under private/.
  • CalibForge: calibforge_environment, calibforge_fixtures, calibforge_native_references, calibforge_captured_fixtures, calibforge_equivalence and calibforge_release inventory, freeze, compare and package fixtures; calibforge_rebuild lowers recipes onto pinned bases.

Docker images these tools commit are host-local until an operator publishes them; exports record image IDs in local-images.json.

Lessons from earlier campaigns

  • Expect most first attempts to fail on job submission, credentials or grading before they touch the data. Use a new report directory for each attempt.
  • An inventory-only source reaches production only through a FULL campaign that publishes a snapshot containing it. Run it on a small runnable source if nothing else needs curating.
  • A failed campaign can move the catalog's CURRENT pointer. Read the report before loading.
  • Credentials given to the driver pod do not always reach the worker pods its coordinator starts. Check that the workers receive them.
  • Use an iris client that matches the deployed controller.
  • Retrying a failed review step returns the same cached judgments unless the grader or cache key changes.
  • Merging Atlas code changes nothing in production until someone runs marina release.

Terms

Agentic task
A task whose agent works in a machine: a shell, files or tools. Reply-only and conversation tasks need no agent machine.
Harbor
A task-directory format and runner: one directory per task with task.toml, an environment and a verifier.
TaskCompendium
Marin's task library and format; its TaskSpec is the canonical record of one task.
Oracle, golden
A reference solution. A golden control grades it and expects reward 1.
Controls
Grader checks before admission: golden scores 1, empty or wrong scores 0.
Oversight level
The weakest review an admission rests on: none, sample or full.
Snapshot (catalog)
One published state of the curation catalog. The Atlas serves one at a time.
Snapshot (Daytona)
A prebuilt sandbox environment. Each unique agent or grader environment is one.
Cohort
A named set of admitted tasks published together as a versioned release.
Selection recipe
A JSON file that names sources and quotas for training and pins the heldout set.
Iris, Zephyr, Marina
Marin's job scheduler, dataset-processing framework and internal app host.
